messages.author: 478aaa6f3786970d
messages.subject: Gaussian mixture model in PyStan
parts:
I'm a novice at PyStan, and I'm attempting to build a model to infer the budget of individual customers from their spending history. Each individual customer budget is drawn from a distribution of budgets, which means that this is a hierarchical model (as I understand it). I have a basic model (see code below) working. Most of it is based on the partial pooling examples in the "Primer on Bayesian Multilevel Modeling using PyStan" by Chris Fonnesbeck.

My question involves extending the model to the case where the distribution of budgets is itself a mixture of two Gaussians. (I believe the customers are actually comprised of two different sub-populations)

Specifically, I want to replace this line (see code below):

budget ~ normal(mu_budget,sd_budget);

with something like this:

budget ~ theta*normal(mu_budget[1],sd_budget[1]) + (1-theta)*normal(mu_budget[2],sd_budget[2]);

although I'm pretty sure this is not correct syntactically.

I have looked at the mixture model examples in the Stan documentation but these seem to involve updating the log_posterior directly; I'm not sure this is what I want to do. Any help would be appreciated! Also, I'd appreciate any comments on the model itself and if the syntax/logic is correct.


Code for working model:

stan_model_simp = """
data {
  int<lower=0> N_customers;
  int<lower=0> N;
  int<lower=1,upper=N_customers> customer_idx[N];
  vector<lower=0.0>[N] actual_spend;
}

parameters {
  real<lower=0.0> mu_budget;
  real<lower=0.0> sd_budget;
  vector<lower=0.0>[N_customers] budget;
  real<lower=0.0> eps;
}

transformed parameters {
  vector<lower=0.0>[N] predicted_spend;
 
  for (i in 1:N)
  {
    predicted_spend[i] <- budget[customer_idx[i]];
  }
}

model {
  mu_budget ~ normal(0.0, 100.0);
  sd_budget ~ normal(0.0, 100.0);
  eps ~ uniform(0.0, 10.0);
  budget ~ normal(mu_budget,sd_budget);
  actual_spend ~ normal(predicted_spend,eps);
}
"""

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Gaussian mixture model in PyStan
parts:
The compiler will test your syntax for you.

You're describing the canonical normal mixture for which
you want to follow the instructions in the manual for
incrementing the target directly. The ~ notation is
just shorthand for incrementing the target density.

- Bob
